name: Skin Micro Motion
algorithm: Skin Micro Motion — Sensor/Physical Model Analyzer
mechanism:
This method analyzes skin micro-motion for deepfake detection:

1. **Micro-Motion Amplification**: Subtle skin surface movements are amplified using Eulerian video magnification or phase-based motion amplification. This reveals sub-pixel movements invisible to direct observation — physiological signals encoded in skin surface dynamics.

2. **Pulse Wave Detection**: The cardiac pulse produces a wave of skin displacement traveling from the heart through arterial branches. This pulse wave should be detectable on the face (particularly at the temporal artery region, neck, and forehead). The method checks for pulse wave presence and propagation consistency. Deepfakes lack physiological micro-motion.

3. **Respiratory Motion Signal**: Chest and shoulder respiratory motion may produce subtle cascading movements visible on the neck and lower face. The method detects respiratory-frequency micro-motion in appropriate facial regions. Absence of respiratory micro-motion indicates AI generation.

4. **Micro-Motion Spatial Coherence**: Physiological micro-motion should be spatially coherent — neighboring skin regions show correlated micro-motion from the same underlying physiological source. The method checks spatial coherence of detected micro-motion. AI generation may produce spatially incoherent micro-motion (independent noise per pixel/region).

5. **Micro-Motion Frequency Spectrum**: Natural skin micro-motion has characteristic frequency content: cardiac (1-2 Hz), respiratory (0.2-0.33 Hz), and physiological tremor (8-12 Hz). The method analyzes the frequency spectrum of amplified motion. AI-generated micro-motion may lack these characteristic frequency components or show wrong frequency signatures.
parameters:
Analysis type: sensor
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through skin micro motion analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
